answer.rationale: Finance's 18% cut mandate cannot be met by the incumbent, who has already refused to reopen price this cycle, ruling out renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms as viable this cycle. The primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so defer_decision risks an uncovered supply gap—unlike the prior non-critical deferral in memory_c5, this contract is critical to line operation. memory_c2 indicates the low-cost vendor previously delivered a sharp cost cut with quick, accurate onboarding, directly supporting switch_primary_vendor as the option that satisfies the mandate. However, the line is running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, so any onboarding friction with a new vendor carries real delivery risk that memory_c2's single favorable instance may not fully capture—hence verifying its archived source before committing. memory_c3 (second-sourcing survived a shortage) is relevant as a risk-mitigation pattern but doesn't by itself resolve the expiring primary contract or meet the cost mandate, so it's noted as a next-cycle consideration rather than this cycle's action. Proceeding with switch_primary_vendor at a standard (not maximal) rollout scale lets us capture the mandated savings while explicitly flagging and monitoring the delivery-risk exposure created by tight capacity during vendor transition.
